question: Should OpenClaw enforce plugin private-import boundaries as a fail-closed loader/runtime security boundary now, or redesign this PR first around current main's plugin loader, SDK resolver, and upgrade path?
rationale: The PR intentionally changes plugin trust and load behavior, but the current implementation has concrete security bypasses and compatibility fallout that automation cannot safely accept as product policy.

options.title: Redesign before merge
options.body: Require a rebased implementation that closes the bypasses, covers dependency and runtime resolution, documents migration expectations, and proves upgrade behavior for existing plugins.

options.title: Accept fail-closed risk
options.body: A maintainer may deliberately land a stricter policy with known plugin breakage and documented limitations, but the security bypasses still need explicit acceptance or removal.

options.title: Pause this branch
options.body: Keep or close this branch as a design spike and replace it with a narrower current-main PR when the permanent plugin boundary contract is decided.

recommendation.title: Redesign before merge
recommendation.body: Require a rebased implementation that closes the bypasses, covers dependency and runtime resolution, documents migration expectations, and proves upgrade behavior for existing plugins.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc owns the PR and has recent plugin SDK/loader boundary history directly tied to the proposed policy.
